title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 222 (Agent to be indemnified against consequences of lawful acts)

content.overview: Section 222 provides that the employer of an agent is bound to indemnify him against the consequences of all lawful acts done by such agent in exercise of the authority conferred upon him.
content.glance: Lawful acts within conferred authority → employer must indemnify the agent against the consequences.
content.study: The employer of an agent is bound to indemnify the agent against the consequences of all lawful acts done by the agent in exercise of the authority conferred upon him. Illustrations: (a) B at Singapore, under instructions from A of Calcutta, contracts to deliver goods to C; A fails to send the goods; C sues B; B defends with A’s authority and pays damages and costs — A is liable to B; (b) broker B, by A’s orders, contracts to buy oil for A; A refuses the oil; C sues B; B defends unsuccessfully after informing A — A is liable to B for damages, costs and expenses. Read with s. 223 (good-faith acts) and s. 224 (no indemnity for criminal acts).

sections.heading: Employer of an agent
sections.body: The principal (employer) of an agent is the party bound to indemnify.

sections.heading: Lawful acts within authority
sections.body: The acts must be lawful and done in exercise of the authority conferred upon the agent.

sections.heading: Duty to indemnify
sections.body: The employer is bound to indemnify the agent against the consequences of those acts.

provisions.title: Agent to be indemnified against consequences of lawful acts

examples.title: Statutory illustration — defence of suit
examples.body: Agent contracts under principal’s instructions; third party sues agent for breach after principal fails to perform; agent defends with authority and pays damages. Principal must indemnify.

hypotheticals.question: Does section 222 cover unlawful acts done in good faith?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 222 requires lawful acts within authority. Good-faith acts that injure third-party rights are addressed under s. 223. Criminal acts are excluded by s. 224.

distinctions.title: Lawful acts within authority (s. 222) vs good-faith acts injuring third parties (s. 223)
distinctions.right: Good faith; may injure third-party rights

misconceptions.trap: The agent always bears the cost of defending third-party claims arising from authorised contracts.
misconceptions.correction: Section 222 requires the employer to indemnify the agent for consequences of lawful acts within authority.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 222 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm agency and conferred authority. II. Test whether the acts were lawful. III. Apply indemnity for consequences. IV. Distinguish ss. 223–224 if good faith or criminality is raised. V. Conclude.
